::: {#exr-holm-threshold}
#### A rejected true null hypothesis has a small p-value under Holm's procedure

Let $m$ null hypotheses have p-values, and let $\truenulls$ be the set of $m_0 \ge 1$ indices of the true null hypotheses.
Show that if [Holm's procedure](#def-holm) at level $\siglevel$ rejects at least one true null hypothesis,
then the smallest p-value among the true null hypotheses is at most $\siglevel / m_0$:

$$\min_{j \in \truenulls} p_j \le \frac{\siglevel}{m_0}.$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {#sol-holm-threshold}

Order the p-values as in @def-holm,
and let $r$ be the smallest rank held by a true null hypothesis,
so that $p_{(r)} = \min_{j \in \truenulls} p_j$.

1. Every hypothesis ranked before $r$ is false,
   and there are $m - m_0$ false null hypotheses, so

   $$r - 1 \le m - m_0.$$

2. Adding $1 - r + m_0$ to both sides of the inequality in step 1 gives

   $$m_0 \le m - r + 1.$$

3. Holm's procedure rejects hypotheses in rank order, $H_{(1)}, \ldots, H_{(k^* - 1)}$.
   A true null hypothesis has rank at least $r$,
   so rejecting one means $k^* - 1 \ge r$, that is $k^* > r$.
   Rank $r$ is therefore before the first failure, and

   $$p_{(r)} \le \frac{\siglevel}{m - r + 1}.$$

4. Step 2 gives $m - r + 1 \ge m_0$,
   so $\siglevel / (m - r + 1) \le \siglevel / m_0$.
   Combining this with step 3,

   $$p_{(r)} \le \frac{\siglevel}{m_0}.$$

Since $p_{(r)} = \min_{j \in \truenulls} p_j$, the claim follows.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#lem-holm-threshold}
#### A rejected true null hypothesis has a small p-value under Holm's procedure

Let $m$ null hypotheses have p-values, and let $\truenulls$ be the set of $m_0 \ge 1$ indices of the true null hypotheses.
If [Holm's procedure](#def-holm) at level $\siglevel$ rejects at least one true null hypothesis,
then the smallest p-value among the true null hypotheses is at most $\siglevel / m_0$:

$$\min_{j \in \truenulls} p_j \le \frac{\siglevel}{m_0}.$$

:::

::: proof
This is the solution to @exr-holm-threshold, worked in @sol-holm-threshold.
:::
